agree.reason: The letter names the Eastside closure up front, gives a concrete doubling offer, and promises to report back, so it could win back a moderately unhappy donor; a reader still angry about the closure gets an acknowledgement but no reason to see the decision differently.

honest.reason: It drops the brief's unsupported claim that a gift guarantees every waiting child a place, presents the full match as conditional ('if we reach'), and every figure traces back to the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out useful figures from the brief ($85 becomes $170, $575 matched pays for one child, $30,000 funds 26 children), but it never says that 61 children would cost about $70,150, and it doesn't use last year's $1,240 to show how much of a stretch the match is.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative, that every child it can't fund stays on the waiting list, is accurate and plain, though it never says that even the full match leaves 35 children waiting.

qualification.reason: The match has a firm cap and deadline ($15,000, December 31), and the January report gives the reader something to check, but the letter doesn't say what happens to any part of the match nobody claims.

objections.reason: It names the closure grievance respectfully but only steps around it: it gives no reason for the closure and doesn't say whether these lessons reach families on the Eastside, which is the real objection for this reader.

fit.reason: It is a year-end email of about 210 words with a subject line, a call to action and the executive director's signature, as the brief asked, and it rightly leaves out the 'guarantee' claim the facts can't support.
